paragraph: Single-family is the market in Ridgefield Park, with 30 sales over six months at a median of $617,500 and a sale-to-list ratio of 1.02. Two thirds of homes sold above list, but the median took 30 days to get there, so this reads competitive rather than frenzied. Priced homes are moving and sellers are getting their number, they are not always getting it in a week. The range runs from $375,000 to $980,000, wide enough that the median is the better guide than either end. Multi-family is small but sharp, 6 sales at a median of $857,500, a 1.08 ratio and a median of 13.5 days on market, which tells you the two-family stock here clears fast when it comes up. Condos and townhouses barely register with 3 sales at a median of $475,000, and co-ops account for 4 at $162,750 with a median of 64 days on market. Co-ops carry board approval, financing restrictions, and resale friction, which not every buyer is aware of going in. On the monthly numbers, most months carry only three or four closings, too thin to call a trend, though July's 12 closings at $608,250 land right on the six-month median, which is steady where a seasonal softening would be normal. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family, the income side of a multi-family, or the lower price point of a co-op.
